In the Craftax game, a partially observed and procedurally generated environment, refinements via episode level feedback stall at <1% final-level arrival, whereas with the feedback cascade the optimized policy reaches the final stage 50% of time (28% final boss defeats). Furthermore, to make this competence reusable towards new goals, we factor the previous controller into an environment interpreter $I$ (models, memory, skills) and a rule program $p_0$, and we show that coding agents can optimize a reusable goal compiler $C_θ$ that maps structured tasks $g$ into new rule programs $p_g$. Across five independent compiler searches trained only on short tasks, the resulting compilers successfully transfer zero-shot to longer tasks without any task-specific tuning nor inference-time LLM calls: continuation-scored feedback and a fixed machine with an editable program together turn a single-task competent policy into a reusable one. Code at: https://github.com/vicgalle/craftax-program-policies

papers.title: Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents
papers.abstract: AI coding agents now push code, publish packages, call model APIs and operate cloud resources on behalf of developers. They authenticate to these services with the same bearer secrets humans use, personal access tokens, API keys and package-registry tokens, stored where the model, its subprocesses and any co-resident malware can read them. Incidents in 2025 and 2026, including prompt-injection attacks on coding agents and self-propagating supply-chain worms, show that this arrangement fails in predictable ways. Passkeys solved the analogous problem for humans, but they require a human gesture on every use and cannot be operated by an autonomous process. We present the Agent Authenticator, a design that gives agents passkey-grade authentication properties: per-service hardware-bound keys, no shared secrets, origin binding enforced by the runtime rather than the model, normalized attestation of the execution environment, human-signed scoped mandates, and cross-device human approval for high-risk actions. The same protocol serves agents on developer laptops and in cloud enclaves, and it deploys as a profile over existing mechanisms, MCP authorization, OAuth token exchange including the Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant, git and SSH, rather than as a new identity system. The authenticator also produces a signed, hash-chained record of each action it authorizes. We analyze the design against a threat model centered on prompt injection and same-host compromise, map it onto five documented incidents, and discuss its limits.

papers.title: Cooperative Gradient Estimation for Multi-Robot Source Seeking with Heteroskedastic Measurements
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for localizing the source of a three-dimensional scalar field using a team of heterogeneous cooperative mobile robots. Each robot measures the field intensity at its location and shares the information within the team. Measurement noise is explicitly considered, and heterogeneity arises from robot-dependent sensing accuracies, leading to heteroskedastic data. The proposed framework combines a weighted centroidal Voronoi tessellation-based formation strategy, defined on a spherical surface and parameterized by sensor noise variances, with a Weighted Least Squares estimator to compute the field gradient at the formation center. By explicitly accounting for sensor heterogeneity in both formation design and estimation, the method achieves robust gradient estimation under noisy measurements. In particular, we show analytically that this construction is nearly optimal. The covariance of the gradient estimate is derived in closed form, providing a lower bound on the attainable estimation variance for any formation on the sphere, and the proposed tessellation is shown to asymptotically satisfy the conditions under which this bound is attained. The estimated gradient is then exploited within a gradient-ascent strategy to guide the team toward the source location. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to alternative strategies and highlight its intrinsic ability to reconfigure online in response to robot failures, thereby enhancing its adaptability.

papers.title: Depth-Aware Path Planning and Collision Avoidance for Robotic Nursing Assistants Using Real-Time 3D Vision
papers.abstract: This paper presents a depth-aware path planning and collision avoidance framework for the safe navigation of robotic nursing assistants in cluttered environments with low-height obstacles. Conventional LiDAR-based navigation systems, while accurate for mapping and localization, fail to detect transparent or low-height obstacles, whereas vision-based systems are prone to noise and occlusion. The proposed framework integrates RGB-D depth sensing, rule-based obstacle avoidance, and the NavfnROS global path planner to drive the robot from an initial point to a goal point. The proposed approach is implemented on the Husky A200 robot, equipped with a Kinova Gen3 arm, to form a complete setup for a robotic nursing assistant. This system features a multi-layer architecture for global planning, perception fusion, and real-time control in the ROS-Gazebo environment. Experimental evaluations in a simulated cluttered environment demonstrate up to 40\% higher success rate and 35\% improvement in minimum clearance compared with single-sensor baselines. Furthermore, real-world experimental results validate the proposed approach as a computationally efficient and safety-aware navigation solution for autonomous healthcare robots.

papers.title: Compiling Imperative Hardware Protocol Specifications to Hardware
papers.abstract: Correct modular composition in hardware depends on interfaces with subtle multi-cycle timing behavior, yet such protocols remain difficult to specify, test, and debug. Recent work has demonstrated that hardware communication specifications can take the form of compact imperative programs that describe the cycle-by-cycle behavior of each logical transaction. However, prior tools only use these specifications for simulation-based testing and debugging, and their semantics remain informal. In this work, we develop a theory of hardware protocol specifications using automata. In addition to making the specifications' meaning precise, the automaton representation lets us compile them into synthesizable hardware. We implement a compiler that produces RTL modules for driving hardware interfaces and for reconstructing logical transactions from low-level I/O signals. We demonstrate a variety of use cases for synthesizable protocol drivers and reconstructors, including runtime monitors that check security properties in the Wishbone protocol and a binding generator that synthesizes interfaces between RTL modules and programs in the Calyx intermediate language.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $σ$-evolution equation $$u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-Δ)^σu+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(τ)/b(τ) dτ$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(τ)/b(τ)dτ\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

papers.title: Geometrically formal Hermitian metrics on compact complex surfaces
papers.abstract: We classify compact complex surfaces admitting either a geometrically Dolbeault formal or an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric. Furthermore, we prove that on a compact Kähler surface, every ABC-geometrically formal metric is Kähler, whereas, for geometrically Dolbeault formal Hermitian metrics, Gauduchon, LCK, and Kähler conditions are equivalent. On non-Kähler surfaces, an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric is LCK and, except on Inoue surfaces, Vaisman.

papers.title: LLM Trading Agents Earn Beta, Not Alpha: A Look-Ahead-Free Benchmark
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents now trade stocks for their users, and benchmarks rank models by their agents' returns. Yet a single run's return says little about skill. In our study, two runs of the same model that differed only in the random seed ended 5.2 points apart on average, so telling skill from luck takes many backtests across markets, models and seeds. However, live arenas trade each day only once, and backtests either use the few months after a model's training cutoff or run on years the model may remember, often with news joined to prices by calendar date. In this paper, we present rta-bench-1, a backtest over three US markets (a rally, a bear market and a crash). It shows each headline only after its publication minute, plays each period blind and named, and checks every run for look-ahead. It also splits each return into factor exposure and alpha and scores every decision against random choices of the same day and sector. In 91 runs of six models from four vendors, no alpha was significant, market and style exposure accounted for a median 78% of the return, and the decisions did no better than random stocks of the same sector. The agents bought the stocks with the most positive news, yet in ablations they earned as much without their headlines. Still, the agents carried out rules reliably, since a single cash rule in the prompt cut a GPT-based agent's share in stocks by 30.3 points in all six pairs. Builders should therefore supply the edge themselves and report exposures and alpha, and benchmarks should replay news by publication time.

papers.title: Ultra-CAN: A Lightweight Blind ISAC Receiver for Chaos-Based Telemetry and Local-Seed Ranging in the Internet of Drones
papers.abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) needs secure telemetry and proximity sensing within the SWaP-C constraints. We show that a single blind neural receiver driven by one chaos-based waveform performs both functions without a separate radar transceiver. In telemetry mode it decodes a peer's burst blindly; in radar mode it regenerates the per-burst chaotic reference locally and ranges the echoes of its own transmission. Ultra-CAN pairs a shared $64$-dimensional representation with two ultra-light backbones, an attention-pooled Conv1D network and a multi-head QKV network ($27.6$k--$44.2$k parameters), feeding communication and sensing heads. Both ship as int8 TensorFlow Lite Micro firmware; the Conv1D receiver decides a burst in $16.9$ ms on a $240$ MHz microcontroller with $24.2$ KiB of activations, a measured energy of $2.2$-$3.4$ mJ per burst, and float-equivalent decisions, sustaining up to $59$ bit/s of telemetry or a $7.4$ Hz range track. The two variants rank first and second among learned demodulators in four aerial swarm scenarios, with a pooled BER down to $4.6 \times 10^{-4}$ on the single-echo link ($2.4 \times 10^{-3}$ with three echoes). Its sensing head identifies true obstacles in $66.8\%$ of peer-laden bursts (vs $42\%$ matched filtering, $44\%$ OFDM-ISAC, $48\%$ peak-picker ceiling). A peer-exclusion gate cuts peer reports from $4.4\%$ to $0.02\%$ of answered bursts, answering $23.5\%$ of total bursts ($75\%$ on the exact tap) with $0.70$ m/s velocity tracking. In-domain refitting recovers telemetry BER by up to three orders of magnitude under 3GPP channels, jamming-aware training restores the link, and frequency agility adds a $6$--$9$ dB margin against partial-band jamming.

papers.title: Edgeworth expansion on sums of Wiener chaos
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Edgeworth expansions for random variables belonging to a fixed finite sum of Wiener chaoses. Building on the work of Mansanarez, Poly and Swan (arXiv:2510.14002) for a single Wiener chaos, we investigate the extension of their approach to functionals $F$ living in a finite sum of Wiener chaoses $\mathcal{W}_{\leq d}$. Within the Malliavin--Stein framework, we bound the total variation distance between the law of $F$ and its Edgeworth approximation of order $2dm$ by $(\sum_{p,q}^d \operatorname{Var}Γ(F_p,F_q))^{m/2}(\operatorname{Var}Γ(F,\operatorname{L}^{-1}F))^{1/2}$, where $F_p$ denotes the projection of $F$ onto the $p$-th Wiener chaos. The presence of several chaotic components introduces additional interactions, since these components are orthogonal but generally dependent. Since our proof relies on the integration-by-parts formalism and the spectral properties of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator, this result extends naturally to the broader framework of Markov chaoses.

papers.title: PathLoop: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Reasoning for Evidence-Grounded Whole-Slide Image Analysis
papers.abstract: Analyzing whole-slide images (WSIs) requires combining evidence across tissue regions and spatial scales. Multi-agent systems offer a promising approach to this task. However, existing systems make limited use of molecular evidence, often select visually prominent but less representative regions while overlooking global context, and struggle to reuse experience from previous cases. To address these challenges, we present PathLoop, a self-evolving multi-agent framework that integrates omics data for evidence-grounded WSI analysis. Specifically, PathLoop coordinates visual and omics interpreters across slide, patch, and pixel levels, using molecular signals to guide region selection and combining local tissue details with global slide features. A judgment agent then checks the consistency of the collected evidence against Pathology-Wiki, a knowledge base built from 48 entries across 24 organ systems, and triggers re-examination when the evidence is inconsistent. To reuse past experience, a four-level memory stores reasoning trajectories, practical tips, skills, and tools to guide future cases, forming a loop of evidence collection, review, and memory update. We evaluate PathLoop on four TCGA cohorts with biomarker prediction, survival prediction, and subtype classification. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of PathLoop across these tasks and support its use for evidence-grounded WSI analysis.

papers.title: Accounting for Attrition in Respondent-Driven Sampling Cohort Studies
papers.abstract: Respondent-driven sampling (RDS) is widely used to recruit populations lacking conventional sampling frames. Because RDS oversamples well-connected individuals, weights are commonly applied to improve representativeness. Although methods for cross-sectional RDS analyses are well developed, guidance for longitudinal studies is limited, despite additional selection bias from missed visits and dropout. We develop a framework that jointly accounts for unequal inclusion probabilities at recruitment and attrition during follow-up. The approach combines baseline RDS weights with inverse-probability-of-non-response weights estimated from observed follow-up histories, producing visit-specific weights for estimating prevalences, means, and regression parameters. We clarify when the RDS design should inform attendance models rather than being addressed only during outcome analysis. Using simulations of RDS recruitment, we assess prevalence and standardized prevalence differences under varying recruitment and attrition mechanisms, focusing on bias, variance, and confidence interval coverage. Weighting the response model by baseline RDS weights was important when an unmeasured determinant of degree also predicted response, even when it did not predict the outcome. We illustrate the framework using data from the Montreal site of Engage, a multisite RDS cohort of sexual minority men in three Canadian cities, from 2017-2023. Follow-up involved intermittent missed visits, attrition, and terminal dropout that was more common among participants with smaller networks. Our findings provide practical guidance for combining design-based and attrition adjustments to support valid inference in longitudinal RDS studies.

papers.title: Objectify, Don't Delete: Complaint-Derived Evaluation of Ambient Clinical Notes
papers.abstract: Evaluating the quality of AI-generated clinical notes is hard: standard metrics like ROUGE measure lexical similarity to reference notes, while expert checklists encode what committees believe matters. Neither captures what clinicians actually complain about. Recent work has shown that evaluation criteria can be mined from user feedback and filtered to criteria that LLM judges can reliably enforce. We argue that this is where much of the value is lost. The criteria that fail enforceability are disproportionately the ones clinicians raise most often, because high-frequency complaints are stated as several questions glued together. No yes/no judgment can grade such composites as posed. We introduce an objectification step that rewrites such criteria into sets of scoped, determinate decisions. We demonstrate the approach through an evaluation pipeline that mines criteria from complaints, objectifies them, and deploys LLM judges against both planted defects and production notes. Across eleven defects planted into ACI-bench reference notes, objectified judges localize violations with median recall of 0.95, while reference metrics change by at most 0.037. Given the complaint as one broad question, the same judges still find every planted defect, but they also flag 70% of the unperturbed reference notes; one section-pair question per call raises Youden's J from 0.30 to 0.72 (by 0.19 to 0.26 with prompt effort matched). We release ACI-Defect, a perturbation benchmark; clinician-reviewed instance-level labels showing quality gaps in the ACI-bench gold standard (32 of 40 notes contain hallucinations; 40 of 40 omit discussed facts); and grounding-judge verdicts. On 1,446 production notes, mean instance-rate burden falls at every clinician-rating step (rho=-0.15), a small association. Defect counts have to be kept per span rather than collapsed into one pass/fail bit per note.

papers.title: Geodesics and a Hubble Relation in Nonstationary Thermodynamic Geometry
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic geometry offers a versatile lens from equilibrium to nonequilibrium, yet typically assumes a stationary metric. Here we study nonstationary thermodynamic geometry, where the metric evolves even at fixed control parameters. The resulting temporal connection generalizes the geodesic equation and redistributes dissipation along optimal control paths. We further establish a thermodynamic Hubble relation that distinguishes relaxation toward equilibrium from geometric expansion or contraction. Brownian examples demonstrate that externally modulated friction can reduce minimum dissipation, while heat exchange with a finite reservoir can induce geometric contraction and Mpemba-type relaxation. Our framework lays a geometric foundation for understanding complex evolving nonequilibrium systems.

papers.title: Geometric Stability and Sample Complexity for Compositional Function Priors
papers.abstract: We study when compositional structure yields dimension reduction in supervised learning. We frame learning as empirical risk minimization with a function-space prior: a regularization functional selects a subset of functions with favorable approximation and metric entropy. The models are compositions $f(x)=g(Ax+Δh(x))$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times d}$ is a linear base map, $Δh$ is a nonlinear correction, and $g$ is an outer function; that is, $f$ is an arbitrary smooth function of a $k$-dimensional representation of the input that is linear up to a correction. We prove covering-number bounds showing that the statistical complexity of this class interpolates between an intrinsic regime, parametric in the $kd$ entries of the linear map and nonparametric only in the representation dimension $k$, and an ambient $d$-dimensional nonparametric rate; the interpolation is controlled by the correction size $\varepsilon=\|Δh\|$. We then connect $\varepsilon$ to data geometry. If the data lie in a small tube around a $k$-dimensional manifold and the regression target depends on the input only through its nearest point on that manifold, then locally the target factorizes exactly as $g(Ax+Δh(x))$ with $A$ a tangent chart and a correction whose Sobolev norm scales linearly with curvature at the localization scale. Patching such local models over an atlas gives a finite-sample excess-risk bound for a least-squares estimator over a finite net of local models, whose ambient term vanishes with curvature. For a one-dimensional model problem we also prove a converse: on curved data, every affine compositional predictor faces an error floor unless its correction budget scales with curvature, while the matching curved model class attains the intrinsic rate. The correction size $\varepsilon$ is thus the effective-dimension parameter linking curvature to statistical complexity.

papers.title: Scalable composite likelihood inference for directed probit networks
papers.abstract: We develop scalable estimation and inference for directed probit networks with correlated sending and receiving effects and residual reciprocity. An incomplete composite likelihood in two stages combines exact bivariate margins of sampled dyads and triples, avoiding integration in high dimensions and cubic enumeration. For fixed parameter dimension, criterion evaluation is linear in the number of draws. Averaging a fixed number of fits from independent index samples reduces sampling variation and allows parallel computation. We establish consistency and joint asymptotic normality with different directional rates, allowing a singular node projection when draw counts lie between the node and dyad scales. An overlap covariance accounts for network and index variation and is consistent relative to each directional variance. Independent index samples stabilize covariance estimation without refitting. The resulting procedure provides standard errors, mapped joint regions and score tests for zero variance components. Simulations show improved estimation from averaging and substantially lower computation times than default Bayesian fitting. An application to a fly brain network with 21,738 neurons demonstrates estimation and inference at a scale relevant to modern network data.

papers.title: A note on distributive lattices with a commutative generalized implication
papers.abstract: We study distributive lattices with an ideal-valued generalized implication satisfying a commutativity identity. This class extends commutative weak Heyting algebras by allowing implication values to be non-principal ideals. We characterize its intersection with several known classes of gi-lattices, study gi-deductive systems and their relationship with gi-filters and gi-congruences, and extend the relational characterization of commutativity to this setting. The resulting correspondence yields a Priestley-style duality by restricting the established duality for gi-lattices.

papers.title: Simulations of turbulent heat and particle transport in stellarator plasmas
papers.abstract: Achieving sustained energy production in magnetic confinement fusion reactors requires a deep understanding of turbulent transport of heat and particles. This thesis investigates turbulent transport with a particular emphasis on stellarators, using simulations with the $δf$ gyrokinetic code stella for the W7-X, LHD, TJ-II and NCSX stellarators, the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak and the Cyclone Base Case (CBC). It addresses two questions: how do density gradients affect turbulent heat transport, and can turbulence help retain particles in the plasma core? In the first part, an inter-machine study shows a strong reduction of the ion heat flux in NCSX and W7-X with increasing density gradients, attributed to the stabilization of ion-temperature-gradient-driven modes without significantly destabilizing trapped-electron modes or universal instabilities. This beneficial effect is absent in tokamaks, where the heat flux increases with the density gradient, highlighting the role of magnetic geometry. The ion heat flux in stellarators does not follow the growth rate of the fastest-growing linear mode, underscoring the importance of nonlinear effects. Trapped-electron modes dominate in CBC, AUG, TJ-II, LHD and NCSX, while passing-particle-driven universal instabilities contribute significantly in W7-X. The second part addresses the long-standing discrepancy between the strongly hollow density profiles predicted by neoclassical theory in large stellarators and the flat or weakly peaked profiles measured in W7-X. Nonlinear simulations and a particle balance analysis show that turbulence provides a robust inward particle flux, driven by finite ion and electron temperature gradients, that can account for the observed profiles: the sign of the turbulent particle flux matches the sign of the discrepancy between the experimental and neoclassical fluxes across the entire plasma radius of W7-X.

papers.title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
papers.abstract: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field. Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations. In particular, we provide a QRF interpretation of the additional gauge-invariant nonlocal separation line obtained from the Cho--Duan--Ge (CDG) reduction reported in lattice simulations of the radially fixed fundamental $SU(2)$ gauge--scalar model. We explain why such a candidate nonlocal boundary is compatible with Fradkin--Shenker continuity and Osterwalder--Seiler analyticity for the appropriate class of local gauge-invariant observables. Separately, we show that a Wilson-rooted control observable admits an exact results at zero plaquette coupling and that it does not cause such a nonlocal separation line.

papers.title: Equilibrium measures for anisotropic exponential interaction energies with applications to transformers
papers.abstract: We study the minimization of anisotropic exponential interaction energies over probability measures on the sphere, motivated by mean-field models of self-attention in transformer architectures. For every symmetric positive definite interaction matrix, we relate the minimizer to a corresponding anisotropic Brownian motion and use the Feynman--Kac formula and elliptic regularity theory to show that it admits a smooth, strictly positive density on the sphere. We further show that it is the only stationary measure with full support for the dynamics considered. We use the stochastic viewpoint to derive an algorithm for sampling from the minimizer. In dimension two, we also propose a numerical scheme for approximating its density based on a Mathieu series expansion.

papers.title: Renormalization Group Flow from 4d Chern-Simons Theory
papers.abstract: The four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory coupled with surface defects is known to realize two-dimensional integrable quantum field theories (QFTs). We discuss the renormalization group (RG) flow of such two-dimensional integrable QFTs from first-principles Feynman diagram computations intrinsically in the four-dimensional framework. We first derive the one-loop RG flow of two-dimensional QFTs realized by the four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory on $Σ\times C$ coupled with the order surface defects supported on $Σ$. Here, the affine Kac-Moody symmetry of the defects underlies the one-loop RG flow. We then derive the one-loop RG flow of the principal chiral model (PCM) without Wess-Zumino term, which is realized using disorder surface defects, within the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. We obtain the nontrivial one-loop RG flow of the PCM, reproducing its known asymptotically-free beta function, using two complementary methods: by explicitly evaluating one-loop Feynman amplitudes, and by computing an analogue of analytic torsion for four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory.

papers.title: Denoising-Induced Recovery of Effective Dynamics
papers.abstract: Recovering dynamical equations from data is a central problem in nonlinear science. In practice, measurements are corrupted by noise and often contain fast oscillations that are not part of the slow dynamics of interest. For this reason, data are typically pre-processed before model recovery or classsification. Here, we reveal the effects of filtering, a specific denoising technique, on recovery. Our analysis show that equation discovery performed on filtered data recovers, up to a fixed precision, the normal-form (effective) equations rather than the original system.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Semantic Alignment via Dual Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Semantic communications enable task-oriented information exchange, but suffer from latent-space mismatch when transmitter and receiver employ heterogeneous machine learning models. Existing semantic alignment methods rely on digital processing, introducing computational and latency overhead. This paper proposes a dual stacked intelligent metasurfaces (dual-SIM) architecture that performs semantic alignment entirely in the wave domain. By jointly exploiting programmable metasurfaces at both ends of a link and the wireless channel, the proposed architecture realizes an end-to-end linear transformation between heterogeneous latent spaces. We show phase-only multilayer SIM can approximate both supervised linear aligners and zero-shot Parseval-frame equalizers. We investigate single-SIM, disjoint asymmetric and symmetric dual-SIM, and jointly optimized dual-SIM configurations, considering channel equalization and constructive channel exploitation. For joint design, we develop an alternating projected gradient algorithm with convergence guarantees to first-order stationary points. We further introduce a deep-unrolled network that unrolls gradient-based iterations to reduce computational cost of SIM reconfiguration under channel variations. Numerical results with heterogeneous vision transformer encoders show accurate semantic alignment from moderate to high signal-to-noise ratios. The joint and symmetric disjoint dual-SIM designs achieve the highest accuracy over compact channels, the joint design leads at shallow stack depths, and the advantage over single-SIM designs diminishes at equal depth.

papers.title: Homomorphisms between Weyl modules for $\mathrm{GL}_3$ in characteristic $2$
papers.abstract: We classify the homomorphism spaces between Weyl modules for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. We prove that these spaces have dimension at most one and give an explicit recursive procedure that determines when they are nonzero and constructs generators in terms of semistandard tableaux. As a consequence, we determine the dimensions of certain homomorphism spaces between Specht modules in characteristic $2$.

papers.title: Local field shifts and the Gribov-Zwanziger horizon functional
papers.abstract: We study a Maggiore-Schaden-like re-centering of the Gribov-Zwanziger action using a smooth compactly supported profile. At fixed background and finite cutoff, under the stated coercivity and contour hypotheses, this transformation preserves the original horizon functional with no residual dependence on the profile. The extension to gauge-field integration requires additional domination assumptions. Near a self-adjoint first Gribov horizon, the response depends on both the lowest Faddeev-Popov eigenvalue and its source weight. We extend this visibility analysis to non-self-adjoint compressions, separating source darkness from truncation-induced shielding, and recall continuum transverse $SU(2)$ examples. Transporting the composite insertion preserves the regulated Gaussian and resolvent structure. A separate free-space tree-level check reproduces the auxiliary-mass denominator of the RGZ propagator, without determining condensate dynamics

papers.title: Sada-ASR: A Production Multidialectal Arabic Speech Recognition System
papers.abstract: Callers to Arabic customer-service lines speak their own dialect, while speech recognizers are built and evaluated mainly on Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). A recognizer that mishears the dialect breaks the call before anything else can help. We present Sada-ASR, the speech recognizer of EchoNova's production Arabic voice agent. On a 120-hour test set of MSA and eight dialects, it has the lowest word and character error rates of twelve systems, against eleven from Microsoft, ElevenLabs, Google, OpenAI, Speechmatics, IFM, Cohere, NVIDIA and Audar: 11.69% word error rate against 13.51% for the strongest, Microsoft's MAI-Transcribe-2 (a lead of 0.74 points on clips unaffected by that system's fixed number and script conventions), and 15.52% against 16.96% averaged over varieties. Its largest margins are on Omani (4.30 points), Egyptian (3.78) and Saudi (2.19) speech; it is level on Syrian and loses on Lebanese (24.96% against 23.05%), mostly because it writes Lebanese words in MSA forms and is less verbatim. On six public test sets its average word error rate under the leaderboard's current scoring is 17.17%, below every published figure we found, among them Falcon-ASR (20.92%), Jais-ASR (22.85%) and Audar-ASR-V1-Turbo (23.17%), though none of these states that it used that scoring, so the comparison is indicative. We describe the data pipeline and methodology behind Sada-ASR and release a 20-hour subset of the test set with our scoring code.

papers.title: DBHiCo: Dual-Branch Hierarchical Contrastive Learning for MRI Image Classification
papers.abstract: Automated Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) image classification provides a crucial non-invasive approach for neurological diagnosis, yet it is fundamentally challenged by inherent acquisition noise and high inter-subject structural similarity, which obscure subtle pathological variations, thereby limiting the performance of deep neural networks. While contrastive learning (CL) offers a promising mitigation strategy, existing paradigms rely on rigid binary partitions that ignore negative sample heterogeneity, and they fail to capture the cross-view structural consistency vital for fine-grained anatomical alignment. To address these barriers, we propose Dual-Branch Hierarchical Contrastive Learning (DBHiCo), a novel framework explicitly designed to collaboratively enforce structural consistency and semantic discrimination. Specifically, DBHiCo leverages a natural anatomical multi-view pair (original and skull-stripped MRI scans), processing them through a dual-branch architecture to seamlessly integrate holistic structural robustness with localized intracranial details. Crucially, we introduce a hierarchical contrastive loss that discards conventional binary constraints in favor of a margin-ranked similarity hierarchy. This mechanism explicitly orders positive and negative pairs based on their structural and semantic difficulty, thereby amplifying the fine-grained semantic discriminability of the learned representations. Extensive experiments across three diverse neurological datasets demonstrate that DBHiCo achieves state-of-the-art performance, consistently outperforming existing MRI multi-view representation learning and advanced contrastive fine-tuning methods.

papers.title: Scalar charge of neutron stars and accreting black holes in Starobinsky gravity: quasi-universal relations, the trace anomaly and gravitational-wave sensitivity
papers.abstract: The Starobinsky scalaron is sourced by the trace of the stress--energy, so its exterior charge is set by the matter around an object and not by the object's vacuum geometry. We derive a master formula for that charge for any static, spherically symmetric source, evaluate it first for neutron stars, where the interior is known, and then for accreting black holes, where it is not. For a star the pressure subtracts: on the interior metric with the Eardley sensitivity, and the charge is a quasi-universal function of the compactness. Six realistic equations of state confirm the relation but lie above the coefficient calibrated on polytropes; the refit reproduces their mean to 0.007. The trace $ρ-3p$ changes sign in the cores of massive stars, and the charge also tracks the tidal deformability and the moment of inertia to a few parts in 1000 and 100. Solving the Einstein-frame structure equations self-consistently moves a star along this relation and leaves its charge at fixed compactness within 4 per cent of the test-field value. We compare the charge with NICER radii and the GW170817 tidal deformability, and use the published massless dipole constraint from GW230529 to calibrate a Fisher estimate of the sensitivity of a similar binary to a finite scalaron range, projected to the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer; the range is a free parameter, and the laboratory bound on pure $R+αR^2$ is confronted explicitly. A vacuum black hole has q=0; a hole with a disc has $q=\sinh(m_ϕr_d)/(m_ϕr_d)$, controlled by the disc's outer edge, which makes it the counterpart in which the same integral is dominated by matter far from the centre; light is blind to the charge at leading order, and the correction beyond it is negligible for any self-consistent disc.

papers.title: Formalizing Formal Semantics: The Formal Atlas
papers.abstract: In this paper we present the Formal Atlas, a system for the study of natural language semantics using proof assistants. Our aim is to formalize semantic accounts, check their predictions and compare the implemented theories. To this end, we connect source records and formal developments with an interactive application, where researchers can inspect proofs and modify supported Rocq files. Montague's PTQ and Gallin provide our main cases, followed by dynamic and type-theoretic comparisons, RSA and distributional semantics. We also discuss what it takes to formalize less explicit analyses. Lastly, we consider the use of AI, both for assistance in developing these resources and for inference systems that can make use of them. This work extends an earlier programme in proof-assistant semantics, with research and teaching as complementary uses.

papers.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

papers.title: Evaluating and Improving Natural Language Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Natural language autoencoders (NLAs) are a method for generating natural language explanations of LLM activations. We develop evaluations based on auditing tasks that test the ability of NLAs to surface latent knowledge, identify whether a model was misled by a hint, and catch a silent fabrication. We also develop extensions to NLAs that let them use activation information from multiple layers and positions, let us apply them more effectively to long transcripts, and reduce the number of false claims they make. These extensions result in improvements on both our auditing evaluations and auxiliary evaluations adapted from prior work. We also use the evaluations to study how different auditing capabilities change over the course of NLA training, and find that although every evaluation improves early in training, extended training can hurt performance on some of our auditing evaluations.

papers.title: Quantum periods and threefold flips
papers.abstract: We study regularized quantum periods under birational contractions involving threefold flips. Let $g:X \dashrightarrow X'$ be a birational map between Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities which contracts exactly one prime divisor $E$ and extracts no divisor. We prove that $$ \lim_{r \rightarrow +\infty}\widehat{G}_{X,rE}(t) =\widehat{G}_{X'}(t). $$ The proof uses logarithmically smooth degenerations and positive discrepancies on good resolutions. Compatibility with orbifold invariants is proved using successive quotient-point extractions and the two-component orbifold degeneration formula. We also define stationary descendant invariants of projective terminal Fano threefolds by good resolutions and prove compatibility with a given projective $\mathbb{Q}$-smoothing. The period comparison extends to projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano endpoints under the same hypothesis on the birational map. Its proof compares the endpoints on a common resolution.

papers.title: Formalizing $\mathsf{einsum}$ with Named Tensor Notation
papers.abstract: Einstein notation ($\mathsf{einsum}$) is a widely adopted tensor operation that has proven useful in areas such as machine learning and quantum computing. But it had no formal semantics until recently, and its properties had no mechanized verification. We formalize the denotational semantics of a language of tensors (multi-dimensional arrays) that supports $\mathsf{einsum}$ and repeated tensors ($\mathsf{expand}$). With this semantics, we verify equational rewriting rules about $\mathsf{einsum}$ and $\mathsf{expand}$ that improve the performance of tensor computation. Whereas typical languages use unnamed tensors, whose shape is a sequence of natural numbers, we found it advantageous for mechanization to use named tensors, whose shape is a finite map from names to natural numbers. To our knowledge, this is the first time that the semantics and rewriting rules of $\mathsf{einsum}$ are mechanized in a proof assistant. Our solution is agnostic to proof assistants; we have implemented it in Lean and partially in Agda.

papers.title: Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials
papers.abstract: We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fréchet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

papers.title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
papers.abstract: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $μ$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

papers.title: Relativistic precession around rotating neutron stars. I. Slow rotation: Hartle--Thorne spacetimes, particle orbits and the QPOs of atoll and Z sources
papers.abstract: We study the relativistic precession model (RPM) of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the spacetimes of slowly rotating neutron stars computed from the equation of state (EOS). For four EOSs (WFF1, G3, FSUGarnet and IOPB-I) we solve the Hartle--Thorne equations to second order in the angular velocity and compute the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of the exterior metric without expanding in the spin or the quadrupole. At $1.9\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ the spin-induced quadrupole is 2--4 times that of a black hole with the same spin; it lowers the nodal precession frequency by up to 25 per cent near the innermost stable circular orbit and limits the nodal frequency that any spin can produce. An eccentric, tilted geodesic around a $1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ star spinning at 363~Hz precesses at the epicyclic rates, and the power spectrum of a hot spot on it peaks at the orbital, periastron and nodal precession frequencies. Applied to the atoll sources 4U 1636$-$53 and 4U 1728$-$34, the RPM gives masses of 2.02--$2.15\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and 1.88--$1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. For 4U 1728$-$34 the low-frequency QPO favours stars with large moments of inertia, $I\simeq2.5\times10^{45}$~g\,cm$^{2}$. Without an EOS the QPOs give $M=1.920^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, $j=0.162^{+0.023}_{-0.011}$ and $\bar Q=2.2^{+1.1}_{-0.8}$; a Kerr spacetime with the same nodal frequency would underestimate the moment of inertia by 22 per cent. For the Z sources GX 5$-$1 and GX 340+0 the horizontal-branch oscillations cannot be twice the nodal precession frequency for any of the four EOSs: the fits are driven to spins of 730--745~Hz and to the maximum mass.

papers.title: Latent Molecular Rollout Towards Causal World Models: Direction is Learnable, Amplitude Control is Readout-Dependent
papers.abstract: A molecular world model should predict how structural changes alter physical properties, not merely assign labels to static molecules. We build a latent molecular rollout system on an 8B Qwen3 backbone, trained on 9,202 aqueous experimental pKa pairs from iBonD, and assess its progress toward causal control by auditing three often-conflated capabilities: predictive fidelity through the intended molecular pathway, directional learnability versus amplitude calibration of target-conditioned displacements, and transfer of latent control to decoded structures. After removing textual shortcuts, continuous latent inference achieves a test MAE of 2.087, significantly outperforming direct molecular feature readout (MAE difference -0.276, 95% CI [-0.352, -0.203], p<0.001). A target-conditioned policy reliably learns displacement directions, with a median cosine of 0.577 and 62.8% of 43 held-out pairs exceeding the 0.3 threshold. Amplitude conclusions are strictly readout-dependent. A frozen linear readout yields near-zero amplitude correlation (-0.020), while a nonlinear gradient-based readout recovers relative amplitude ordering (correlation 0.585, sign accuracy 0.744-0.767) with compressed absolute scale. At the decoded structure level, neither input-slot editing nor direct final-state injection produces meaningful changes across 80 test sources, bounding the tested control surfaces rather than indicating a universal decoder bottleneck. Generation fine-tuning shows relative improvement under internal oracle evaluation but does not surpass a simple constant baseline in single-sample settings. These results delineate the capability frontier of fixed-scale latent molecular interfaces: directional control is robustly achievable, but calibrated amplitude control and decoded structural transfer remain open challenges on the path to causal molecular world models.

papers.title: Black holes in Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate vacuum black-hole solutions in metric-affine Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity (MG-I), where $R$ is the affine Ricci scalar and $T$ is a quadratic torsion invariant, not the trace of the matter energy-momentum tensor. For the polynomial model $F(R,T)=αR+βT+γT^3$, with $α\neq0$, we first vary the metric and all components of the independent affine connection, and only then specialize to metric-compatible geometry with totally antisymmetric torsion. Nonzero axial torsion admits an exceptional branch $α+β+3γT_*^2=0$, on which the metric satisfies the Einstein equations with effective cosmological parameter $Λ_*=γT_*^3/α$. We establish a local existence result and construct torsionful Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter representatives that are smooth through a selected future Killing horizon. Within the spherically symmetric axial ansatz, we characterize Ricci-symmetric affine connections by the condition $(fV-U)'=0$ and compare a constant-$W=fV-U$ family with a constant-$U$ family. Although these connections share the same metric and torsion scalar, their affine curvature invariants generally differ. Independent coordinate-level curvature contractions and component tests of the unrestricted metric and connection variations corroborate the identities used in the construction; these checks complement the analytic variational derivation. Finally, we identify null directions of the restricted axial quadratic form and distinguish this degeneracy from a complete metric-affine stability analysis. Our conclusions are local and do not establish global extendibility, physical inequivalence of all torsion profiles, or dynamical stability.

papers.title: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
papers.abstract: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from a covariance-adjusted discriminant to the mean difference, and evaluate probing and additive steering, which adds the direction to the hidden state, along the family at a fixed side effect. For truthfulness and sentiment, in every model, the best probe is not the best steering direction: steering consistently favors directions closer to the mean difference. This separation holds across 59 of 60 layer-model-concept combinations in a layer sweep, with matched probe and steering texts in all six model-concept combinations, and under a rotation-based steering operator. The exact steering optimum is less stable: for sentiment, an intermediate direction produces a 27-56% stronger steering effect than the mean difference, but this gain shrinks or disappears with matched texts and depends on the layer and the operator. The two roles also transfer differently across models. A probe transferred by a linear map fitted on neutral text retains 81-91% of the target model's above-chance probing performance, while the transferred mean difference retains less of its steering effect in 11 of 12 model pairs. This is a consistent tendency, although our predefined criteria classify only three pairs, and nine remain inconclusive. Finally, as an application on PopQA, steering toward "unknown" increases abstention by 18-44 percentage points on uncertain errors, versus 2-5 on confident errors, while rarely correcting errors in cases where a correct answer is reachable.

papers.title: $K_1^*(1870)$ and $3S$-$2D$ mixing in the strange meson sector
papers.abstract: Very recently, the BESIII Collaboration reported the first observation of a $J^P=1^-$ strange resonance in the $Kη'$ system, the $K_1^*(1870)$. We examine whether this state can be accommodated in the kaon meson family. Although it cannot be assigned as a pure $3^3S_1$ or $2^3D_1$ state, we show that it can be described as the lower state of $3S$-$2D$ mixing, whose mass agrees with the measured value, and we predict its higher-mass partner. Using the quark pair creation model, we calculate the OZI-allowed decay properties of both \textcolor{black}{mixed} states; the total decay width of the lower state is consistent with the measured width of the $K_1^*(1870)$. We note that the subordinate $Kη'$ decay mode of this state appears to contradict its observed $Kη'$ decay channel, which calls for further study. We further investigate the production of these two states via the $Kp$ reaction, which may provide valuable information for future experimental searches.

papers.title: Asymptotic Divergence-Based Monitoring for Data Drift in Production AI Systems: A Discrete Case Approach
papers.abstract: We develop a complete asymptotic theory for monitoring data drift in production artificial intelligence (AI) systems whose inputs take values in a finite set of categories. The framework combines two complementary inferential tools. Under the no-drift hypothesis $H_0$, the two-sample likelihood-ratio statistic $G$ of Wilks follows a universal Chi_{r-1}^2 law, independently of the divergence chosen and of the sample sizes; the calibrated Population Stability Index (PSI) of Yurdakul and Naranjo (2021) shares the same Chi_{r-1}^2 limit and is asymptotically equivalent to the $G$-test under $H_0$. Under the drift hypothesis $H_1$, the plug-in phi-divergence is asymptotically normal with a variance computed in closed form for the one-sample, two-sample and symmetrized configurations, yielding standardized $Z$-statistics, detection boundaries, power functions and sample-size planning rules. We supply a per-category decomposition that localizes the drift on specific categories, a Benjamini--Hochberg procedure for monitoring many features simultaneously, and an explicit comparison with the heuristic PSI cut-offs of industrial practice. Two fully worked simulation examples - one one-sample with the Rényi divergence and multiple testing, one two-sample with the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and sample-size planning - illustrate every notion of the paper on realistic production data.

papers.title: Maximality of the Došen--Petrić Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two morphisms differ. Composition with morphisms selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables is a preorder. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.title: Vegetation Health Classification for Low-Data and Edge Hardware Deployment
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with cameras are popular, viable tools for vegetation and environmental health monitoring. However, existing image classification methods are incompatible with UAV implementation for independent practitioners in remote, resource-constrained environments due to large dataset requirements, GPU hardware, inflexible retraining, and low interpretability. This paper presents a lightweight, interpretable vegetation classification algorithm operating with as few as five reference images per class, without GPUs or heavy machine learning frameworks. It uses a 2D hue-saturation histogram feature representation and Earth Mover's Distance or Quadratic Form Distance, paired with a log-likelihood probability score, to classify images into three vegetation health categories. We evaluated six systems: three custom pipelines and three established models across low-data scenarios ($n = 5, 10, 25$) and a full-data regime of 2,172 drone images from 28 South American locations. Our custom pipelines achieve competitive Top-1 accuracy (81--85\%) under low-data constraints, maintaining sub-1ms inference times that enable real-time classification and subsequently tasks such as seeding and watering. The algorithms also support incremental retraining without full model reconstruction. We validate edge feasibility by deploying the QFD variant on an ESP32 microcontroller, achieving 82.8\% accuracy with 1.01\% heap memory utilization (45kb), demonstrating that effective vegetation classification is achievable on low-cost, low-power embedded hardware without cellular connectivity.

papers.title: A quantitative measure of predictability for surface gravity waves
papers.abstract: We introduce a Bayesian inference framework to characterize the predictability of a one dimensional ocean surface wave field given surface elevation measurements from a sensor. Unlike the classical theories that only sketch the boundary of a predictable zone based on group velocity, we use the Bayesian posterior uncertainty of surface elevation to quantify the local predictability at every spatiotemporal location. Our approach first constructs a prior distribution to encode existing knowledge of the wave field such as the spectrum and propagation direction. By conditioning on the (possibly noisy) measurement data, we infer the posterior distribution of the wave field, from which a spatiotemporal uncertainty map is extracted. This map agrees well with the group-velocity-based classical predictable zone theory when the frequency spectrum has bounded support. Meanwhile, it also demonstrates predictability even for a spectrum with unbounded frequency support where the classical predictable zone degenerates. A refined analysis of posterior uncertainty using observability Gramian matrix reveals a `data-informed' part and an `un-informed' part of the wave field, with the latter being fundamentally un-predictable. Furthermore, nonlinear effects can be naturally introduced into the Bayesian framework by incorporating the nonlinear ocean surface wave equations. This is the first time that nonlinearity is rigorously treated in the predictable zone problem. We perform numerical tests using both bounded, piecewise constant spectrum and unbounded JONSWAP spectrum. The numerical results confirm the proposed advantages of our method for linear waves and reveal how wave steepness affects the predictability of nonlinear waves. Nonlinear modal interactions redistribute uncertainty between the inside and the outside of the predictable zone with an amount proportional to the wave steepness.

papers.title: Beyond Paired Inputs: Learning to Leverage RGB-T Cross-Modal Relations in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) sensors provide complementary observations, yet their distinct sensing characteristics make effective cross-modal coordination challenging. Although existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can process paired RGB-T inputs, they often fail to translate cross-modal relations into effective task-specific decisions, leaving the potential of these relations to improve task performance and robustness largely untapped. Motivated by this observation, we introduce RelMLLM, an RGB-T MLLM that explicitly learns to exploit cross-modal relations in task-specific decision making. It represents modality reliability, the cross-modal relation, and the dominant modality as a verifiable decision state. We derive task-grounded supervision for this state by comparing RGB-only, TIR-only, and paired RGB-T task outcomes. A hierarchical relation-guided reward supervises modality-specific evidence, relation-state prediction, and the final task output, while encouraging consistency across evidence, relation, and decision. We evaluate RelMLLM on natural RGB-T grounding, RGB-T visual question answering, and held-out sensor degradation. RelMLLM improves grounding accuracy and degradation robustness over its Qwen3-VL baselines while preserving performance on general RGB-T reasoning benchmarks. These results demonstrate that effectively exploiting cross-modal relations leads to more accurate and robust RGB-T decisions. Code and model weights are publicly available.

papers.title: Quaternion Matrix Tuples with Common Invariant Subspaces: Dimension and Nonuniqueness
papers.abstract: Let $M_n(\mathbb{H})$ denote the algebra of $n\times n$ quaternion matrices. We study common invariant right subspaces of tuples in $M_n(\mathbb{H})^r$ and determine exact real semialgebraic dimensions for two associated sets. If $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ are positive integers, $n=n_1+\cdots+n_s$, and $q=\sum_{1\leq a<b\leq s}n_an_b$, the set of tuples preserving at least one nested chain with successive increments $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)q$. For $r\geq2$ and $1\leq k<n$, the set of tuples with at least two distinct common $k$-dimensional right invariant subspaces has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)(k(n-k)+n-1)$. The proofs use finite right-module coordinates and a common local-rank argument.

papers.title: Unbound matter in the circum-halo medium: a common mediator of halo secondary bias
papers.abstract: Halo secondary bias describes the dependence of halo clustering on properties beyond mass. Here we report that a new environmental metric, the unbound matter fraction ($f_{\rm un}$) in the $2$--$3\,R_{\rm vir}$ shell around a halo, can largely account for secondary bias. Using haloes with $M_{\rm vir}=10^{10.5}$--$10^{14.5}h^{-1}{\rm M_\odot}$ at $z=0$ obtained from TNG300-1-Dark, we find that controlling for $f_{\rm un}$ reduces the secondary bias of formation time, concentration, spin, shape and velocity anisotropy to a residual correlation of $\lesssim 4\%$, outperforming other environmental metrics such as the tidal anisotropy for spin and velocity anisotropy. Applying a stacking method to the circum-halo medium (CHM), we identify two distinct flow patterns: low-$f_{\rm un}$ haloes co-move with coherent flows, with the CHM converging onto the haloes; in contrast, high-$f_{\rm un}$ haloes move through dynamically hot, partially virialized structures, with the CHM passing by rather than being accreted. This dichotomy points to two distinct regimes of secondary bias, a `cold' regime and a `hot' regime, in which tidal and inertial forces act as the main drivers, respectively, with the dominant mechanism migrating from the former to the latter as haloes assemble into massive structures. At fixed large-scale environment, $f_{\rm un}$ further indicates the presence of nearby neighbours and the competitive accretion. Our results highlight the role of unbound matter as a mediator of environmental effects on haloes, and reveal the physical mechanisms that shape the CHM pattern through which these effects are mediated.

papers.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining scalar spectral flow on fixed spaces with overgroup nullities, we bound the number of bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and singular ambient endpoints, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. Finite Morse index reduces the inputs to indices and nullities; extensions cover varying form domains and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. For a Newtonian nine-body family containing a reported counterexample to Moeckel's stability conjecture, we prove analytically that two nonconjugate exact reflection types bifurcate at a common central mass, displacing the central body. Positivity excludes larger stabilizers, while a scalar Schur complement synchronizes the bifurcations, independently of the reported stability assertion.

papers.title: Sustaining In-Network Computation in Satellite Networks: An Architecture for Semantic Continuity
papers.abstract: Satellite computations often outlast the paths and providers initially serving them. We argue that in-network computing should organize changing execution opportunities around one continuing logical computation: workers execute ready operations, while consumers recognize which results already contribute. We present an architecture separating logical computation, stream context, and physical binding, and show in wildfire assessment how retained observations support recomputation while reachable association history stays in place. A 300-node Linux prototype examines placement, dependency assembly, and continuation. Across 120 images, stage-wise placement delivers 82.08% of positions within deadlines versus 76.06% for single-node placement, while traces separate blocked output delivery from dependencies split across providers. Across 50 observations with 20-node isolation, Confirmation-Coordinated Rebinding (CCR) coordinates replanning, source replay, cross-attempt acceptance, and in-band confirmation to complete all 50 observations with verified outputs using seven replays and 13 ignored duplicate outputs.

papers.title: Ship-as-a-buoy for Phase-resolved Reconstruction of Surface Waves
papers.abstract: We develop a data assimilation framework to address the ``ship-as-a-buoy'' problem, i.e., estimation of the wave field from time series of ship motion. Unlike previous algorithms which only provide information of wave spectrum, our approach reconstructs the instantaneous phase-resolved wave field. The full framework includes two steps: the first step to generate an initial (rough) estimation of the wave field using the response-amplitude-operators (RAOs), and the second step to refine the reconstruction using an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) to incorporate the measured motion time series. Together with EnKF in the second step, we model the coupled wave-ship dynamics by a high-order spectral (HOS) method for waves and a Cummins equation for ship motion (although higher-fidelity ship model can be applied). We conduct extensive tests of our method for the case with one ship, and the naturally extended cases with multiple ships or with uncertain parameters in the ship motion model. For all test cases we demonstrate favorable reconstruction of the wave field, which in general further improves with the number of ships available and with uncertain parameters properly estimated. We also provide insights on the successful reconstruction in terms of ensemble correlations between the motion time series and features of the wave field.

papers.title: Self-similarity of axisymmetric Marangoni flows on a deep viscous subphase
papers.abstract: Local gradients of surface tension caused by inhomogeneous distributions of surfactant molecules are known to generate Marangoni flows, the mechanics of which have important consequences in various areas of science and engineering. In this paper, we investigate the deposition of insoluble surfactants on the surface of a deep, viscous subphase, which propagate axisymmetrically without diffusing. We study these flows from the perspective of self-similarity, i.e., seeking solutions which show universal features on appropriate length and time scales. We first present a closed form, self-similar solution of the first kind for the axisymmetric spreading of surfactants, which is globally valid at long times. We then numerically study `filling' flows of surfactant, where the surfactant distribution is locally depleted such that inward flows are generated to `fill' the surfactant-free area. These flows have the special feature of forming cusp-like structure in finite time, which have been studied extensively in the literature of self-similarity of the second kind. We show that these flows admit a countably infinite number of stable similarity solutions based on the local behavior of the initial surfactant concentration profile. We remark on a few unique features of these results in contrast to filling flows in other physical limits.

papers.title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
papers.abstract: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $ν>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of $1.5\times10^{-13}$ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.

papers.title: PALIN: Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR Multimodal 3D Object Detection with Benchmark
papers.abstract: 3D object detection is critical for intelligent transportation systems. LiDAR has been widely adopted for accurate geometric measurements; however, purely geometric representations remain ambiguous under sparse observations and occlusions, while cross-sensor multimodal fusion suffers from calibration and synchronization errors. To overcome these challenges, we leverage an Ouster LiDAR to construct PALIN (Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR), a large-scale intrinsically pixel-aligned multimodal dataset jointly capturing geometry and NIR intensity, comprising approximately 8,000 annotated frames from static urban intersections and diverse mobile suburban scenes. Building upon this dataset, we propose CMambaFusion, a novel fusion framework consisting of a four-directional Cross-Mamba module for bidirectional cross-modal interaction and a Gated Concat-Mamba module for joint feature refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PALIN enables effective multimodal learning, and CMambaFusion achieves superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs over both LiDAR-only and representative fusion baselines.

papers.title: Leveraging Dual-Process Theory for Multimodal Multiparty Turn-Taking Prediction
papers.abstract: In multiparty conversations, a pause does not always mean a speaker has finished, and another voice does not necessarily indicate a change in who holds the conversational floor. Reliable turn-taking therefore requires recognising not only whether a speaker is ready to yield the floor, but also when a possible transition deserves attention. We propose a dual-process-inspired framework that separates continuous candidate discovery from selective verification. A fast, recall-oriented stage identifies plausible transition points. In contrast, a deliberative stage combines acoustic, linguistic, speaker-related, and predicted future-activity evidence, together with multimodal cues where available, to reject false candidates and refine transition timing. We evaluate the framework through three distinct tasks: SHIFT/HOLD classification at supplied decision points, verification of automatically generated candidates, and continuous discovery and localisation of floor transfers. On VoxConverse, we derive action-aware turn-taking events from speaker-diarization annotations to examine unconstrained conversations with varying numbers of speakers. Multi-TPC provides complementary evaluation of controlled triadic interactions using speech, gaze, motion, and prosodic information. The findings reveal that identifying plausible transitions is considerably easier than reliably confirming and localising genuine floor transfers, while the contribution of individual evidence sources varies across conversational settings. These results highlight the importance of treating multiparty turn-taking as a continuous discovery-and-verification problem rather than classification at predefined boundaries.

papers.title: Bright-Dark State Interplay Governs Vibronic Decoherence in Molecular Aggregates
papers.abstract: In this study, we establish a spectroscopy-driven framework that connects optically bright vibronic eigenstates to their subsequent decoherence dynamics in excitonic molecular aggregates. Combining the Multiparticle Holstein Formalism with explicit system--bath interactions, we demonstrate that relaxation-induced purity loss is governed by three interconnected factors: (i) the bath spectral window, which determines the accessibility of intra- and interband relaxation pathways; (ii) the local network of dark vibronic states surrounding the optically prepared bright state; and (iii) the energetic placement of the bright state, which controls downhill relaxation. Remarkably, states with different excitation energies exhibit nearly identical purity dynamics when their local relaxation networks are similar. The resulting H--J asymmetry further reveals the importance of energetic directionality. These findings establish a reliable connection between optical spectroscopy, vibronic band structure, and state-selective loss in purity.

papers.title: UACS: Uncertainty-Aware Clustering and Sparse Parameter Estimation for Multi-Condition Wheel Center Force
papers.abstract: Accurate wheel center force (WCF) estimation is important for vehicle durability analysis and condition monitoring, whereas direct measurement requires dedicated transducers and increases instrumentation cost and complexity. As a result, soft sensors have attracted considerable attention as a practical alternative. However, developing reliable soft sensors remains challenging due to varying working conditions, unknown condition relationships, and high-dimensional model representations. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware clustering and sparse parameter estimation framework (UACS) for WCF signal estimation under diverse and unlabeled working conditions. A MISO-FIR model is first constructed using easily accessible sensor signals to estimate the unmeasurable force signal. The uncertainty of estimated parameters is quantified through confidence ellipsoids, and pairwise hypothesis testing is developed to identify statistically similar working conditions. Based on these uncertainty-aware comparisons, working conditions are grouped in an unsupervised manner, and sparse parameter estimation is performed within each cluster. The UACS framework simultaneously reduces the number of required models and active parameters while maintaining estimation accuracy. Experiments using real-world vehicle data demonstrate that the UACS framework achieves estimation accuracy comparable to condition-specific models while substantially reducing the number of required models and outperforming conventional distance-based clustering approaches.

papers.title: Computing rare events in Lévy-driven systems via optimal control
papers.abstract: We extend the optimal control formulation of sample path large deviation theory, which has proven effective for numerical computation of instantons and sharp probability estimates in stochastic differential equations with Gaussian noise, to systems with light-tailed Lévy noise. In the scaling limit of small jumps and high intensity, such systems satisfy a large deviation principle of Freidlin-Wentzell type, with a running cost given by the Legendre transform of the noise cumulant generating function. We propose to numerically minimize this cost over noise realizations subject to the system dynamics, which yields the instanton without having to solve Hamilton's equations, and naturally handles degenerate and multiplicative noise. When the cumulant generating function has a bounded domain, the cost grows only linearly for large noise, and instantons can contain jumps. We analyze when jumps are not only admissible but optimal, depending on the subleading behavior of the cost and on the drift, and show how jumps can be resolved numerically through a time reparameterization that freezes physical time. For continuous instantons, we derive Riccati and Fredholm determinant expressions for the leading-order prefactor, and we discuss the modifications needed when the instanton jumps. We illustrate and validate our methods against Monte Carlo simulations in several examples: a two-dimensional nonlinear model, an active run-and-tumble particle with non-Gaussian tumbling noise, and the Ghil-Sellers energy balance climate model with Lévy-perturbed solar forcing.

papers.title: Probing SAM Perturbations Through Statistical Replay
papers.abstract: Sharpness Aware Minimization (SAM) updates model parameters using gradients evaluated at adversarially perturbed weights, but it remains unclear which aspects of this procedure are sufficient to reproduce its generalization behavior. In our ResNet 18 experiments on CIFAR 10, simple curvature regularizers based on the Hessian trace and largest eigenvalue remain below SAM in validation accuracy, motivating a direct examination of its perturbations.
